This article from the Harvard Business Review argues that while many companies are looking to democratize access to data, they’re overlooking the fundamental issue of power and privilege. For example, in the healthcare industry, the patient has the most power when it comes to their data, but healthcare companies have the most power when it comes to treating their patients. If healthcare companies begin to treat the data they collect from patients as an asset, rather than as a liability, patients will be able to benefit from the democratization of data on a much deeper level.

A data democracy is not just about access to data, but about how we use it. We must start from a place of respect for the data and the people who produce it. Data democratization is about giving the power of data back to the people it belongs to.
